title: Manoj Bajpayee to Play Mahatma Gandhi in Sudhir Mishra's New Film
excerpt: The film, produced by Anubhav Sinha, focuses on a little-known 21-day period around India's Independence, with filming set to begin in September in Kolkata.
body:
• Manoj Bajpayee will play Mahatma Gandhi in a new feature film directed by Sudhir Mishra and produced by Anubhav Sinha
  • The film focuses on a little-known 21-day period around India's Independence when Gandhi left Delhi, departing from the typical biopic format
  • Saurabh Shukla has been cast in a supporting role, with filming expected to begin in September in Kolkata
  • The project reunites Mishra and Sinha, both known for socially engaged cinema, and marks Bajpayee's first portrayal of the Mahatma

Manoj Bajpayee, one of Indian cinema's most respected actors, will play Mahatma Gandhi in a new feature film directed by Sudhir Mishra and produced by Anubhav Sinha, the filmmakers confirmed this week. The project marks Bajpayee's first portrayal of India's founding father and brings together three of Hindi cinema's most acclaimed figures in socially conscious filmmaking.

A Gandhi Film Unlike Others

Rather than a sweeping cradle-to-funeral biopic — a format most famously executed in Richard Attenborough's 1982 film — the new project will focus on a compressed and lesser-known period in Gandhi's life. The film centers on a 21-day stretch around India's Independence in August 1947, during which Gandhi left Delhi amid the communal violence and political upheaval of Partition.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=gFNxUKpcGzc

The specific historical episode the filmmakers have chosen has received relatively little attention in cinema. While Gandhi's role in the independence movement and his assassination in January 1948 have been extensively dramatized, the weeks immediately surrounding August 15, 1947 — when he was notably absent from the celebrations in Delhi — remain underexplored on screen.

"This is a story that needs to be told — not the Gandhi everyone knows, but the Gandhi who walked away from the celebration of everything he fought for."

— Sudhir Mishra, confirming the project on social media

The Creative Team

Director Sudhir Mishra has built a career on films that grapple with politics, ideology, and social fracture. His filmography includes "Hazaaron Khwaishein Aisi" (2003), widely regarded as one of the finest Hindi films about post-Emergency India, and the more recent "Serious Men" adaptation. His approach to historical material tends toward intimate character study rather than spectacle.

Producer Anubhav Sinha's recent work — including "Article 15" (2019), "Thappad" (2020), and "Bheed" (2023) — has consistently engaged with caste, gender, and systemic inequality. His production sensibility suggests the Gandhi film will prioritize narrative substance over visual scale.

Saurabh Shukla, the veteran actor and screenwriter known for his roles in "Satya," "Raid," and numerous courtroom dramas, has been cast in a supporting role. The character has not been publicly disclosed. Filming is expected to begin in September, with Kolkata confirmed as a primary shooting location.

Bajpayee's Transformation

Bajpayee, 57, has earned three National Film Awards across a career defined by range and intensity, from the gangster Bhiku Mhatre in "Satya" (1998) to the intelligence officer Srikant Tiwari in the "Family Man" series. His filmography includes some of Hindi cinema's most demanding character work, but playing Gandhi represents a departure in both physicality and register.

The casting echoes a pattern in recent Indian cinema where leading actors have taken on historically weighted roles later in their careers. Ben Kingsley's Oscar-winning portrayal in Attenborough's "Gandhi" remains the benchmark, while more recent depictions by Rajkumar Rao in "Gandhi Godse: Ek Yudh" (2023) explored the ideological dimensions of Gandhi's final years.

For diaspora audiences who grew up with Bajpayee's work from the parallel cinema movement through the OTT era, the casting pairs one of Indian cinema's most compelling performers with its most consequential historical figure. How Mishra's characteristically intimate directorial lens shapes the portrayal of a public icon will be closely watched.
